messages.subject: dynamic number of tabs and tab-dependent UI in the sidebar
parts:
Hello, 

This is the continuation of Generating a series of tabs.

I have found a way to put a UI in the sidebar which is dependent on the active tab :

app: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/MetaDynamicUI7bis/ 
code: https://gist.github.com/stla/7334172

In this example the tab-dependent UI is the radioButtons "plot title". Do you think the way I use is a good practice ? 

The piece of code making the tab-dependent UI is :
  Radiobutton <- function(i, selected=NULL){
    radioButtons(paste0("radio",i), "plot title:", choices=c("bonjour", "guten Tag"), selected=selected)      
  }
  output$Radio <- renderUI({
    if (!is.null(pObjects())) {
      i <- input$tab0
      selected <-  if(!is.null(input[[paste0("radio",i)]])) input[[paste0("radio",i)]] else NULL
      if(!is.element(i, c("0","firsttab","summarytab"))){
        return(Radiobutton(as.numeric(i),selected))
      }
    }
  })
I use selected <- if(...  because the selected value of the UI would be automatically reset without this line.

Radiobutton(as.numeric(i), input[[paste0("radio",i)]])

messages.subject: Re: dynamic number of tabs and tab-dependent UI in the sidebar
parts:
Thus finally here is the clean code:

  Radiobutton <- function(i, selected=NULL){
    id <- paste0("radio",i)
    radioButtons(id, "plot title:", choices=c("bonjour", "guten Tag"), selected=input[[id]])      
  }
  output$Radio <- renderUI({
    if (!is.null(pObjects())) {
      i <- input$tab0
      if(!is.element(i, c("0","firsttab","summarytab"))){
        return(Radiobutton(as.numeric(i)))
      }
    }
  })

I think I have found a better method for tab-dependent inputs in the sidebar. 

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/stla/TabDependentWidget/ 

With the old method, the widget is recreated each time the user goes back to a tab :

  ##

id <- paste0("radio",i)

  }

Recall that the dynamic number of tabs J is set at the first step and does not change anymore : it is defined by the dataset selection input at the beginning, which appears only once. All the objects which are dynamic but fixed after the first step are stored in the reactive conductor pObjects(). 
With the new method I store the tab-dependent inputs in a reactive list. Hence, there's no update when the user goes back to a tab: there's only a new rendering of the widget (cause it is tab-dependent), but its content has not changed, whereas the selected value of the widget is updated with the old method.

  ##
  ## METHOD 2 - make a numeric input widget depending on the active tab  (to put in the sidebar)

    if(is.null(pObjects())) return(NULL)
    J <- pObjects()$J
    for(i in as.character(1:J)){
      NUMERICSINPUTS[[i]] <- numericInput(paste0("num",i), "set a number", value=input[[paste0("num",i)]])
